identity.title: Suitability Filter: A Statistical Framework for Classifier Evaluation in Real-World Deployment Settings

problem.claim: Safety-critical deployment requires assessing downstream model reliability when user-data ground-truth labels are unavailable.

gap.claim: Direct validation of deployed performance is limited by the absence of ground-truth labels on user data.

contributions.claim: Introduces the suitability filter, which uses output-derived suitability signals sensitive to covariate shift to detect possible performance deterioration.
Defines deployment evaluation as testing whether unlabeled-user accuracy degradation relative to labeled-test accuracy stays within a pre-specified acceptable margin.
Aggregates suitability signals across test and user data and compares their empirical distributions through hypothesis testing to characterize decision uncertainty.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the suitability filter as a novel framework for evaluating classifier suitability without labeled user data.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that evaluations across different classification tasks reliably detected performance deviations caused by covariate shift.
The authors report that the framework enables proactive mitigation of potential failures in high-stakes applications.

narrative_sequence.summary: Unlabeled user data makes direct validation of safety-critical model performance difficult.
The paper proposes suitability signals and the suitability filter to identify possible degradation under covariate shift.
The filter checks whether degradation relative to labeled-test accuracy exceeds a pre-specified acceptable margin.
Distributional hypothesis testing supplies decision-uncertainty information, while the modular method is intended for varied models and domains.
Across classification tasks, the authors report reliable detection of covariate-shift-related deviations and support for proactive failure mitigation.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns an unlabeled deployment decision with a measurable tolerance margin and explicitly reports decision uncertainty from distributional testing.

lessons.interpretation: A deployment-oriented evaluation claim becomes more actionable when its acceptance rule and uncertainty signal are specified together.
lessons.application: For a method evaluated under distribution shift, state the operational pass/fail margin and the statistical quantity used to express uncertainty.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when no defensible tolerance can be defined or when output signals are not meaningfully shift-sensitive.

unknowns: The abstract gives no numerical results, task details, or baselines for the reported evaluations.
The pre-specified margin, suitability-signal construction, hypothesis test, and conditions behind the reliability claim are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish that the proposed framework prevents failures or that its stated novelty is prior-art verified.
